verdict.rationale: DeepSeek's docs say coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and OpenCode can use it as a backend directly with no code. It also offers OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs for the existing SDKs, a function-calling guide, and a DeepSeek Harness developer preview for agent harness developers. However, the integrations rely on API compatibility rather than first-party skills, plugins or a native SDK, and named agent-framework integrations are not documented. missing for 10: first-party skills or plugins for coding agents, a native DeepSeek SDK, documented official integrations with agent frameworks (e.g. LangChain, LlamaIndex), Harness details beyond a preview announcement, independent hands-on corroboration of the agent integrations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug the model into coding agents and agent frameworks through documented, official integrations — skills, plugins, or first-class SDK support

citations.quote: If you use tools like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or OpenCode, you can use DeepSeek as the backend model directly — no code required.
By modifying the configuration, you can use the OpenAI/Anthropic SDK or softwares compatible with the OpenAI/Anthropic API to access the DeepSeek API.
DeepSeek Harness is now in developer preview for agent harness developers worldwide.
A maintained function-calling guide with runnable OpenAI-format examples (stream or non-stream) — tool use is a documented first-class capability of the API.
